Rashi on Arakhin 4b:10:1.hebrew: אלא קרא - בערכך למאי אתא? הואיל וערך סתם אינו אלא ג' שקלים, בלא קרא נמי ידענא, דבלא כלום לא מיפטר, ובציר מהכי לא מצי יהיב, דהא אין ערך קצוב נקרא בפחות מיכן:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:10:1.english: Rather, the verse - For what did "[according to] your valuation" come? Since an unspecified valuation is only three shekels, even without a verse I would know [this], for he is not exempt with nothing, and less than this he cannot give, as there is no fixed valuation stated at less than this.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:10:2.hebrew: שאינו נידון בהשג יד - שאפילו אין ידו משגת לג' שקלים, נותן ג' שקלים:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:10:2.english: That he is not judged according to [his] means - That even if his means do not suffice for three shekels, he gives three shekels.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:10:3.hebrew: כמפרש דמי - דכיון דאמר ערך סתם עלי, ויודע הוא שזהו פחות שבערכין — ג' שקלים — כמאן דאמר הרי עלי ג' שקלים דמי. ולא דמי לאומר ערכי עלי או ערך פלוני עלי, דהתם לא מוכחא מילתא, דאין הכל יודעין את שנותיו; אבל הכא דבר גלוי הוא, שהרי לא תלה בשום אדם:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:10:3.english: It is considered as though he explicitly specified - For since he said, "An unspecified valuation is upon me," and he knows that this is the minimum of the valuations — three shekels — it is considered like one who said, "Behold, three shekels are upon me." And it is not similar to one who says, "My valuation is upon me" or "The valuation of so-and-so is upon me," for there, the matter is not evident, as not everyone knows his age; but here, it is an evident matter, for he did not make [it] dependent upon any person.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:11:1.hebrew: איכא דאמרי א"ר נחמן - להכי אתא קרא, לומר שערך נקרא, ודינו כשאר ערכין, ונידון בהשג יד:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:11:1.english: There are those who say Rav Naḥman said - For this [purpose] the verse came: to say that it is called a valuation, and its law is like [that of] other valuations, and it is judged according to [one's] means.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:11:2.english: [It is] obvious - For in what way is it different from other valuations?

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:12:1.hebrew: קרי ביה ערך בערכך - ערך הוה מצי למכתב, והוה מייתי ערך סתם. ומדכתב ערכך — למדרש נמי הא:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:12:1.english: Read into it: "Valuation," "according to your valuation" - [The verse] could have written [simply] "valuation," and that would have derived an unspecified valuation; and since it wrote "your valuation," [it is] to expound this [ruling] as well.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:16:1.english: To say below - To include a disfigured [person] and one afflicted with boils.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:19:1.hebrew: הא אפיקתיה להנך - לאחד שהעריך את מאה, ולאשה שהעריכה:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:19:1.english: Behold, you have applied it to those - [Namely,] to one who valuated a hundred [people], and to a woman who valuated.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:20:1.hebrew: שקול הוא - אי הוה כתיב נמי נפש, הוו אתו כולהו: בין דבר שהנשמה תלויה בו, בין אחד שהעריך מאה, ובין אשה שהעריכה — דנפש משמע אשה, ומשמע נפשות הרבה, כענין שנאמר (במדבר ל״א:ל״ה) ונפש אדם מן הנשים ששה עשר אלף. ואע"ג דמחד נפש לא מצינו למדרש ג' דרשות, הוו אתו כולהו, דהא שקולים הן ושוות ונשמעות ממקרא זה, ולא מצית לאוקמה להא דרשא טפי מהא; והי מינייהו מפקת? הלכך, כולהו אתו מיניה, ונפשות איצטריך למנוול ומוכה שחין, דלא תימעטינהו מנדר בערכין:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:20:1.english: It is balanced - Even if it had only written nefesh [in the singular], all of them would have been derived: whether [an organ] upon which life depends, whether one [person] who valuated a hundred [people], or whether a woman who valuated — for nefesh implies a woman, and it implies many people, as it is stated (Numbers 31:35): “And human persons of the women were sixteen thousand.” And even though from one [word], nefesh, we cannot derive three expositions, all of them would be derived, since they are balanced and equal and indicated by this verse, and you cannot apply it to this exposition more than to that [exposition]; and which of them would you exclude? Therefore, all of them are derived from it; and nefashot was needed for a repulsive person and one afflicted with boils, so that you would not exclude them based on [the juxtaposition of] “a vow” and “valuation.”

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:20:2.hebrew: שקול - שוה. דכל הדרשות שוות למשמע ממקרא זה, ואין לך חומר בזו יותר מזו דנימא: הך קא מרבה לחודה, והך — שקולין הן. איכא נמי בב"ק (דף ג.) כי האי גוונא בשמעתא קמייתא:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:20:2.english: Balanced - [Meaning] equal. For all the expositions are equally implied by this verse, and you have no greater stringency in this one than in that one, such that we would say: It includes this one alone, and [what of] that one? They are equivalent. There is also in Bava Kamma (3a) [an argument] like this in the first sugya.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:21:1.hebrew: לדמים - דאם אינו ענין לערכין — דהא זכר ודאי בעינן — תניהו ענין לדמים:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:21:1.english: For monetary value - For if it is not applicable to [fixed] valuations — since we require a definite male — apply it to monetary value.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:22:1.hebrew: שנידון בכבודו - שנידון כולו אחר אבר אחד שכבודו תלוי בו, שאם אמר ״דמי ראשו עלי״, נותן דמי כולו:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:22:1.english: That he is judged according to his dignity - That his entirety is judged according to a single limb upon which his dignity depends, such that if one said, “The value of his head is upon me,” he gives the value of his entirety.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:23:1.hebrew: ה"ג סד"א נדר בערכך נפשות כתיב כל שישנו בערכין נידון בכבודו - אפי' כשאמר דמי ראשי עלי. וכל שאינו בערכין, כשאמר דמי ראשי עלי — אינו נידון בכבודו, דנפשות גבי ערך כתיב — קמ"ל:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:23:1.english: This is the correct reading: You might have thought to say: "A vow according to your valuation, souls" is written; whoever is subject to valuations is judged according to his vital part - [That is,] even when he said, "The value of my head is upon me." And anyone who is not subject to valuations, when he said, "The value of my head is upon me," is not judged according to his vital part, because "souls" is written in connection with "valuation" — [therefore, the verse] comes to teach us [that he too is judged according to his vital part].

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:24:1.hebrew: משמנין ביניהן - כמה שוה, ויחלוקו דמיו. ומבעיא לי: אמאי נקט התם ״שותפין״, והכא ״משמנין״:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:24:1.english: They appraise between them - [They evaluate] how much it is worth, and they divide its value. And it is a question for me: Why did [the baraita] use [the term] 'partners' there, and 'they appraise' here?

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:25:1.english: And Rav Pappa said - [He explains] what the reason is that in the case of a cow, he consecrated only its head.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:25:2.hebrew: דהא מזדבן ריש תורא בבי טבחא - אבל ראש עבד וראש חמור אין דרך למכור. הלכך, לפלגיה זבניה, לפלגיה אקדשיה:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:25:2.english: For the head of an ox is sold in the butcher shop - But the head of a slave and the head of a donkey are not customarily sold [separately]. Therefore, [in the case of sale,] he sold half of him [or it], [and in the case of consecration,] he consecrated half of him [or it].

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:26:1.hebrew: ואין נידון בכבודו - דקתני: הוא והקדש שותפין בו, ולא הוי כוליה דהקדש:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:26:1.english: And is not assessed according to its dignity - For it teaches: "He and the Temple treasury are partners in it," and the whole of it does not belong to the Temple treasury.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:26:2.hebrew: והא עבד דאיתיה בערכין - כדקתני במתני', וקתני בהך ברייתא גבי עבד נמי: ״הוא והקדש שותפין בו״, דאין נידון בכבודו:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:26:2.english: And behold, a slave is [included] in valuations - As is taught in the Mishnah; and it is taught in that baraita regarding a slave as well: "He and the Temple treasury are partners in him," meaning that he is not assessed according to his dignity.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:27:1.hebrew: אלא ל"ק - הך ברייתא דקדשי מזבח, דאמר: ״ראש חמור או עבד זה לדמי עולה״ — אין נידון בכבודו; דכי כתיב ״נפשות״, גבי ערכין כתיב, דקדשי בדק הבית נינהו. וכי קאמרינן אנו דנידון בכבודו — אפילו טומטום — שנדר דמיו בקדשי בדק הבית:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:27:1.english: Rather, this is not difficult - That baraita [deals with] consecrations for the altar, where he said: "The head of this donkey or slave [is consecrated] for the value of a burnt offering" — [and therefore] he [or it] is not assessed according to his [or its] dignity; for when "persons" is written, it is written regarding valuations, which are consecrations for Temple maintenance. And when we say that he is assessed according to his dignity — even [in the case of] a tumtum — [that is where] he vowed his value for consecrations to Temple maintenance.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:28:1.english: Let sanctity spread throughout all of it - Since it is fit for sacrifice.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:3:1.hebrew: נפשות - דהכי משמע: "בערכך נפשות" — כל נפשות יכולות להעריך:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:3:1.english: Persons - For this is what it implies: "According to your valuation, persons" — all persons are able to valuate.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:4:1.hebrew: וכל שאינו בערכין - כגון טומטום ואנדרוגינוס, דכתיב: "הזכר", דמשמע: זכר ודאי, נקבה ודאית:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:4:1.english: And anyone who is not [included] in valuations - Such as a tumtum and an androgynos, as it is written: "The male," which implies: a definite male [and] a definite female.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:7:1.hebrew: ערך סתום - שלא אמר ״ערכי עלי״, ולא אמר ״ערך פלוני עלי״, אלא אמר ״הרי עלי ערך״:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:7:1.english: An unspecified valuation - Where he did not say, "My valuation is upon me," and he did not say, "The valuation of so-and-so is upon me," but rather he said, "Behold, upon me is a valuation."

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:7:2.hebrew: שלשת שקלים - דכתיב: "ולנקבה שלשת שקלים", וזהו פחות שבערכין:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:7:2.english: Three shekels - As it is written: "And for a female, three shekels" [Leviticus 27:6], and this is the smallest of the valuations.

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:8:1.hebrew: מרובה לא תפסתה - דיש להקשות: תפוס את המועט:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:8:1.english: [If you grasped] the greater [amount], you did not grasp [it] - For one can object: "Grasp the lesser [amount]!"

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:8:2.hebrew: תפסתה מועט תפסתה - דאי מקשה לך: ״תפוס את המרובה״, אינו חולק על דבריך, אלא מוסיף, דבכלל מרובה איכא מועט:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:8:2.english: [If] you grasped the smaller [amount], you grasped [it] - For if someone objects to you, "Grasp the larger [amount]," he is not disputing your words, but rather adding [to them], for the smaller [amount] is included within the larger [amount].

Rashi on Arakhin 4b:9:1.hebrew: בהשג יד - שאם עני הוא ומך מערכך, לא יעריכנו כהן בפחות משקל. אבל דין ערך קצוב — אין מועט מג' שקלים:
Rashi on Arakhin 4b:9:1.english: With regard to affordability - That if he is poor and "is poorer than your valuation," the priest shall not evaluate him at less than a shekel; but [regarding] the law of a fixed valuation, there is none less than three shekels.

Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:10:1.hebrew: לומר שאין נידון בהשג יד - מ"ט? "כמפרש דמי": דכיון דאמר "ערך סתם עלי", ויודע הוא שזהו פחות שבערכין, ג' שקלים, כמ"ד "הרי עלי ג' שקלים"; ולא דמי לאומר "ערך פלוני", דהתם לא מוכחא מילתא, דאין הכל יודעין שנותיו, אבל הכא דבר גלוי הוא, שהרי לא תלה בשום אדם — לשון הקונטרס. וקשה: דהא כי אמר "ערך פלוני עלי", יודע הוא שאינו בן חדש וחייב ה' סלעים, ונידון בהשג יד — שבסלע אחד או בשנים?! ונראה לפרש: "כמפרש דמי" — דהוי כמו אומר בהדיא "הרי עלי שלש סלעים", הואיל ואמר "ערך סתם". דודאי אי אמר "ערך פלוני בן עשרים", אף על פי שיודע שיתחייב חמשים סלעים, מ"מ גזירת הכתוב — כיון שתלה הערך בנערך — גזירת הכתוב הוא שידון בהשג יד, ואינו כמו מפרש "הרי עלי נ' סלעים לבדק הבית":
Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:10:1.english: "To say that he is not judged by affordability" - [The Gemara asks:] What is the reason? [And answers:] "It is considered as though he explicitly [specified]": For since he said, "An unspecified valuation is upon me," and he knows that this is the lowest of valuations, three shekels, it is like one who says, "Behold, upon me are three shekels." And this is not similar to one who says, "The valuation of so-and-so [is upon me]," for there the matter is not evident, as not everyone knows his years [i.e., his age]; but here it is an evident matter, since he did not link it to any person — [this is] the wording of Rashi. And this is difficult: For when one says, "The valuation of so-and-so is upon me," he knows that he is not [less than] a month old and is [thus] obligated in [at least] five selas, and [yet] he is judged by affordability — [paying] one sela or two?! And it seems [preferable] to explain: "It is considered as though he explicitly [specified]" — that it is as though he explicitly says, "Behold, upon me are three selas," since he said "an unspecified valuation." For certainly, if he said, "The valuation of so-and-so, who is twenty years old, [is upon me]," even though he knows that he will be obligated in fifty selas, nevertheless it is a scriptural decree — since he linked the valuation to a person being evaluated, it is a scriptural decree that he is judged by affordability, and it is not like one who explicitly specifies, "Behold, upon me are fifty selas for Temple maintenance."

Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:12:1.hebrew: קרי ביה ערך בערכך - מיתורא בערכך, דמצי למכתב ערך, ומיתורא דריש; ואילו ערך גופיה איצטריך:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:12:1.english: "Read into it: Erekh, be’erkekha" - [This is derived] from the superfluity in be’erkekha, as it could have written [simply] erekh; and from the superfluity it expounds [this additional law], whereas [the word] erekh itself was needed [to derive an unspecified valuation].

Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:24:1.hebrew: הוא והקדש שותפין כו' - פי' בקונטרס, דגבי הקדש נקט שותפות, לומר שהוא והקדש חולקין — דמקדיש בעין יפה מקדיש; אבל גבי מכירה שייך דמשמנין, לשון שומא — כלומר, שישומו אותו אבר שמכר לאיזה מלאכה הוא ראוי, ולפי שויה יטול:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:24:1.english: "He and the Temple treasury are partners," etc. - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that regarding consecrated property, [the baraita] formulated "partnership" to say that he and the Temple treasury divide [the value], because one who consecrates does so generously; but regarding a sale, [the term] "they appraise" applies, [which is] an expression of appraisal — meaning, that they appraise that limb that he sold [to determine] for what labor it is fit, and according to its value he takes [his share].

Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:26:1.hebrew: והא פרה וחמור דליתנהו בערכין ואינו נידון בכבודו - וכל שכן כשמקדיש הגוף, דפשטה קדושה בכולה:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:26:1.english: "And behold, a cow and a donkey are not [subject to] valuations, and it is not assessed by its dignity" - And all the more so when one consecrates the body [itself], that the sanctity spreads throughout all of it.

Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:27:1.hebrew: הא לא קשיא הא בקדשי מזבח הא בקדשי בדק הבית - ברייתא — בקדשי מזבח, דאמר: "ראש חמור הקדש לדמי עולה", ואינו נידון בכבודו; דכי כתיב "נפשות", גבי ערכין כתיב, דקדשי בדק הבית נינהו. וכי אמרינן אנו דנידון בכבודו — אפילו טומטום — שנודר לדמיו לבדק הבית:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:27:1.english: "This is not difficult: this [refers to] items consecrated for the altar, while that [refers to] items consecrated for Temple maintenance" - The baraita [deals with] items consecrated for the altar, where [one] said: "The head of [this] donkey is consecrated for the value of a burnt-offering," and it is not assessed by its significance; for when "souls" [nefashot] is written, it is written regarding valuations, which are [consecrated for] Temple maintenance. And when we say that [one] is assessed by his significance — even a tumtum — [that is in a case where] one vows his value to Temple maintenance.

Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:7:1.hebrew: וכמה פחות שבערכין שלשה שקלים - אע"ג דאמר בתוספתא דמכילתין: "הרי עלי ערך סתם — מביא המועט. וכמה (את) המועט? ה' שקלים (סלעים)" — י"ל דהתם בסתם ערך דזכר (ונקבה) הוא:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4b:7:1.english: "And how much is the smallest of the valuations? Three shekels" - Even though it says in the Tosefta of our tractate: "[If one says:] 'An unspecified valuation is incumbent upon me,' he brings the minimum. And how much is the minimum? Five shekels (sela'im)" — one can say that there [in the Tosefta], it refers to an unspecified valuation of a male (and a female) [which is parenthesized for deletion, as five shekels is the minimum valuation only for a male].
